newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal sector wages talks collapse - union.
newsitem.headline: German metal sector wages talks collapse - union.

text.p: Negotiations over a pay dispute in the German metal and engineering sector have collapsed, the head of the IG Metall trade union said on Wednesday.

IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel told a news briefing that talks had broken down between the union and the Gesamtmetall employers federation because the employers had "only fractionally" altered their position during 13 hours of negotiations.
The two sides had been seeking to find agreement on how labour costs to employers could be reduced while putting in place measures to protect existing employment in the hard-hit industry.

Companies in the sector including industrial giant Dainler Benz AG had attempted earlier this month to put through a new law allowing it to cut sick pay allowances to 80 percent of full salary from 100 percent.
But the employers were later forced to back down on the cuts after a day of protest involving more than 100,000 engineering workers and costing them hundreds of millions of marks.
IG Metall said employers had only offered a 1997 wage increase in line with inflation during the latest talks and were demanding that such a rise be accompanied with cuts to labour costs.

The trade union has said it could only accept an inflation-based wage rise if linked with measures to secure employment in the industry, where jobs levels have fallen by around one million to 3.5 million since 1991.
A further nationwide day of protest is now expected to go ahead following the collapse of talks.
